messages.author: cd1835d7cf8edf1d
messages.subject: Calculating Cohen's f2
parts:
Is there a proven approach to take a lavaan model and calculate Cohen's f2?


From the calculation it requires the R-squared of the path (R2ab) and the partial R-squared of all the effects of except the one I'm interested in.


I know how to get the R-squared from a lavaan model, but what I'm having trouble with is how to compute the partial R-squared. The method I've seen in some publications (e.g. Selya et al. 2012) is to run the models without the effects your interested in and get the partial R-squared that way. But in the lavaan model leaving out single effect could cause some issues - the model may become misspecified. Is there a proven way of doing this that won't lead to model specification errors?


Thanks!


Selya, A. S., Rose, J. S., Dierker, L. C., Hedeker, D., & Mermelstein, R. J. 2012. A Practical Guide to Calculating Cohen’s f(2), a Measure of Local Effect Size, from PROC MIXED. Frontiers in Psychology, 3: 111.
